scope.summary: A single Postgres-backed personal platform served as two composed binaries: a private read-write binary (full app capabilities, private.jomcgi.dev) and an isolated public binary (jomcgi.dev via the separate monolith-public chart). The public binary is read-only for public datasets with two constrained write/invocation paths, the private binary now also serves an agent-session console, a six-language code sandbox, a screenshot tool, and MCP over native streamable HTTP; safety is governed data access, bounded public capabilities, the secret boundary, and correct claim/lease ownership of queued agent work.
scope.built: framework/core.py composition and profiles, separate private/public module registries, Postgres leader-lease singletons (Discord bot, AIS ingest, outbox drain, message-lock sweep), the agent_sessions claim-lease turn engine (atomic per-message claiming across all replicas plus a leader-owned stale-claim sweep) backing both the Discord bot and the private factory execution console HTTP API, goosecracker recipe/repo catalog, chat feature ACL with 30s grant cache, public_reader/public_writer roles with schema/view confinement, public/private HTTPRoutes, Turnstile secret isolation, public chat admission/concurrency limits, public FaaS identity gate, observability snapshot rollup, the shotter MCP domain (URL/host validation, EmberVM task dispatch, best-effort authenticated R2 PNG storage with a random per-call Idempotency-Key), the sandbox MCP domain (run_code, six per-language EmberVM task workloads, zero-egress except an optional scratch-Postgres credential), the native /mcp mount on stateless streamable HTTP with PrincipalMiddleware authenticating every message via cached JWKS, and the docs/posts manifest generators that publish an exact allowlist of committed repository documents to the public site. The factory knowledge-graph evidence lanes (#5527, ADR agents/063) add a shared raw-input write boundary (knowledge/raw_write.py persist_raw_with_status) reached by the generic POST /api/knowledge/raws endpoint, three MCP tools (report_knowledge, dispute_fact, report_distress), and a leader-owned Ember-session exporter (factory/execution/kg_feed.py), a daily-capped DBOS drainer (factory/orchestration/drainer.py) that runs Luna extraction in an EmberVM guest and writes atoms with server-side provenance (knowledge/extraction.py, knowledge/atoms.py), and a live disputed/verification_state signal on search results (knowledge/store.py). The shared CNPG backup checker publishes bounded observations through one precreated ConfigMap, the private monolith evaluates their freshness and 36-hour backup age as advisory health, and its leader queues transitions through the existing durable Discord outbox. The default-off backlog refill controller reserves advisory inventory work from fresh intake counts, validates the artifact, publishes through durable per-output intents and records conclusive yield separately from interrupted or uncertain runs. Focused historical learning cessation repair against 434907e17 with this diff: authenticated retained journal proof, fresh successor/restore and local lineage checks, digest/CAS/idempotent audit; no live recovery or activation is claimed.
scope.designed: Strict per-domain database isolation and the ADR 010 cross-domain contract remain architectural goals; the Module/build_app framework itself is built. ADR 059 (Draft) proposes removing Context Forge entirely as the MCP entry point and serving /mcp directly behind Cloudflare; only the first, independently-sequenced slice (the stateless-HTTP transport switch) has landed, Context Forge is still deployed and still in the request path. The shared GroupPolicyMiddleware requires operators for private MCP calls by default; finer tool-specific entitlements remain separate work (#6475).

losses.title: Data is corrupted, or a side-effecting action (Discord post, agent run, chat_public write) is duplicated or forged
A queued turn or locked message never makes progress
An agent acts on incomplete or misattributed context, losing lineage of what it was told
A secret or token reaches a tier or surface that must not hold it
A controller serves stale or wrong data while believing it correct
Anonymous or public-tier caller reads data it is not entitled to (private rows, ungoverned paths)

hazards.statement: An agent turn runs twice: a stale-claim sweep reclaims a lease still held by an actively-executing replica, or a manual resubmission overlaps a guest-side invoke the monolith timed out on without confirming it stopped

X-Auth-Email is forwarded by several allowlisted in-cluster senders (gateway, MCP gateway, Argo job pods, the EmberVM progress-ingest sidecar) that do not all cryptographically bind the claim to a verified caller; today it is read only for attribution (agent_sessions triggered_by), but nothing stops a future authorization decision from keying on it without also verifying the caller's JWT
public_reader is granted on a schema or view that includes non-public rows
A caller treats the derived screenshot URL as a durable readable reference despite a failed R2 write or unestablished read access
A private-tier screenshot outlives its intended use in R2 and remains available to an authorized object reader; application code sets no expiry or deletion policy
The public HTTPRoute forwards an internal or unfiltered path to a served handler
The internet-adjacent public tier can write outside the intended chat_public path, or bypasses Turnstile, per-session limits, and the cluster-wide inference cap

The scratch-Postgres feature, when enabled, injects a database DSN into the executed code's own process environment, so a Python run in the advertised zero-network sandbox gains credentialed, in-cluster network reach to a shared datastore; the tool's own docstring still claims there is no network at all

The monolith-side host/scheme allowlist is weakened, widened without an ADR amendment, or bypassed, letting an out-of-policy top-level URL reach the EmberVM dispatch call; the guest-side in-guest proxy allowlist (projects/embervm/STPA.md) is the actual control on what gets fetched, so this alone does not open egress
A private secret or a K8s token is delivered to the public or frontend tier
Two replicas both believe they are leader and run duplicate bot/ingest/drain
A revoked feature grant keeps authorizing an action from the 30s ACL cache
The public stats endpoint serves an old observability snapshot after the rollup job stops
A caller re-invoking run_code with the same code but different input files receives a cached result computed against a prior submission's files instead of a fresh run

No rate limit gates shotter.capture or sandbox.run, so a caller can queue captures/runs faster than the workload's own cap admits, consuming brick memMib capacity shared with other task-class workloads

The docs/posts manifest generators copy an allowlisted document's full body into the public site verbatim, gating only on which path may be published, never on what the content contains, so an internal-only identifier (a cluster-internal hostname, a secret env var name) left in a published project's README/ARCHITECTURE/STPA reaches the public docs route

The shared operators gate admits an operator to private MCP tools without finer tool-specific entitlements; disabling or bypassing that gate can admit callers outside operators to private capture and other capabilities

A queued agent turn never progresses because no replica ever holds leadership to run the stale-claim sweep, and the replica that would have executed it directly crashed or restarted before claiming it

A credential in a shape outside the fixed patterns in knowledge/redact.py reaches the knowledge lane: persist_raw_with_status redacts known shapes for every lane-owned source, including the generic POST /api/knowledge/raws endpoint and the tools/session_collector claude-session/codex-session producer, then stores and extracts unmatched content verbatim into durable, searchable graph facts

The backup checker stops publishing fresh observations while base backups fail, leaving operators without a backup-failure notification because unknown observations intentionally cause neither a transition nor reminder
An operator treats an observational control-subgate result or missing evidence as permission to dispatch or recover, bypassing fresh execution checks or overlapping an uncertain execution
An operator attributes a historical funding decision or session observation to the wrong current request or canonical attempt, selecting an unsupported recovery or leaving eligible work stalled
A machine landing grant authorizes a PR outside the standing operator's fixed paths, authentic objective provenance or cumulative derivation limits
Restoring policy bytes after a successful or indeterminate transition revives an earlier standing decision or exact-head grant
A PR enters or remains in the merge queue after its head, independent review, CI, holds or execution ownership cease to satisfy the grant
A stale queue observation removes a newly authorized current head or treats an unrelated base advance as a changed reviewed diff
A native brief reporting that no leave-unmerged hold exists is read back as a positive hold, preventing otherwise eligible existing work from reaching its normal delivery controls
A broad comment exemption discards a real or ambiguous hold, or a reader treats absence of a text veto as delivery authority
Enabled required repair discovery never advances retained blocker events because optional scout surplus is incorrectly required despite ordinary permitted quota
Required discovery treats unverified account evidence or a depleted five-hour window as permitted recovery capacity
A retry preparation supersedes the exact attempted receipt named by the first response-loss hold, preventing normal result adoption
A prepared row or cancelled promotion is treated as completed, ceased or never invoked, allowing duplicate execution or unsupported capacity release
Incomplete or stale cessation evidence releases capacity while a different dispatch or replacement guest may still execute
Positively terminal guests predating a local restore failure leave an interactive permit indefinitely uncertain
A repaired native role resumes outside its original unused allocation, current ownership, exact repair proof or finite deadline
An explicit landing grant authorizes source or effects outside the authenticated operator decision and independent typed review

ucas.condition: The reclaim lease and the local heartbeat check are computed from two different clocks (the lease cutoff from the pod's own monotonic-adjacent wall clock, the claimed_at write from the database's); a pod running ahead of the database clock reclaims a lease that is still being actively refreshed elsewhere, and the reclaiming replica's own self-check ('claim was stolen') only protects the replica that LOST the claim, not the window before the next 10s heartbeat catches it, so both replicas can execute the same turn concurrently for up to that window
The public tier accepts a write without the Turnstile/IP-hash admission gate or writes outside the constrained chat_public schema, poisoning or escaping the public boundary

The generator's only gate is an exact repo-path allowlist; it checks documents for certain markers (in-cluster hostnames, 1Password refs, private IPs, node/brick names, S3 URIs, .internal domains, secret env assignments) but internal identifiers not matching these patterns pass through unreviewed
A grant on ALL TABLES or a view lacking the visibility filter exposes private rows to the anonymous tier

An MCP caller with a valid bearer token issues an ArgoCD sync or resource mutation with no additional per-tool authorization of which Principal may trigger it; the delegation seam (#4940) exists but this tool does not consume it
A slow handler still processing past the 30s TTL is reclaimed and the message is reprocessed concurrently
A public HTTPRoute sends an unapproved backend path to the internet, or the frontend SSR proxy exposes a private-only route

When the scratch-Postgres feature is enabled, run_code's own docstring still advertises 'there is no network at all' for every language while the Python path silently gains a credentialed connection string to an in-cluster datastore, so a caller relies on an isolation guarantee the tool does not actually provide for that one language
A private credential, Kubernetes API-capable token, or Turnstile secret is wired into the public frontend or public backend beyond its explicitly constrained use

If MCP_GROUP_POLICY_ENFORCED is disabled or the operator gate is bypassed, a caller outside operators can render private.jomcgi.dev pages; the current GroupPolicyMiddleware denies such calls by default and shotter has no public tag

A private-tier PNG is uploaded without an application expiry or delete path; it may remain retrievable by an authorized S3 reader after its intended use, subject to the bucket lifecycle. The returned endpoint URL is not presigned, and neither indefinite retention nor anonymous hash-based reads are established by this code

HOST_SERVICE_MAP is widened past its documented exactly-two-entries invariant, or validate_screenshot_url is bypassed, without an accompanying ADR amendment; the two allowlists (monolith host map, guest-side hard allowlist) are not tied by any build-time invariant, so they can drift independently

The endpoint accepts up to 2 MiB under any extractable source label except the MCP-owned agent-report and dispute; the shared boundary redacts only the fixed patterns in knowledge/redact.py, so a credential in another shape is enqueued for extraction and indexed as durable private-visibility knowledge notes

Applying owner authority from a stale preview, ambiguous owner identity or changed intake policy would grant unintended scope; standing-human checks, version/digest comparison and a separate idempotent audit bind the exact decision

Applying a repair decision with changed mode, path profile or limits would expand authority; standing-human preview/apply binds version, digest and prior authorization with explicit finite-trial or bounded ongoing mode

Deriving from a copied owner marker, absent accepted objective/refinement, broader diff or reset receipt history would grant unintended or repeated authority; authentic intake, canonical ownership, exact typed review, fixed eight-file profile and three-per-day/three-per-canonical-PR limits are checked under locks

Deriving for a legacy card, recursive repair, unmatched machine pause or replenished task allowance would exceed the decision; exact post-authorization producer/watch provenance, fixed reviewed paths and trial or rolling plus cumulative task/source bounds gate each distinct grant

Arming after a changed head/review, new hold, unknown start or claimed message would use stale authority; derivation and final locked validation share the quiescence guard, reobserve exact review/diff/CI and preserve explicit human-grant precedence

Leaving an armed entry after revocation, expiry, policy transition or failed current-head checks retains obsolete authority; the native observer revalidates known deliveries before eligibility filters and disarms/dequeues invalid entries, with errors retained for later observation

Dequeuing using an observation from before a concurrent authorization would discard valid work; the queue fence re-reads PR identity, queue membership and authority under the same control lock used by grant application

An enabled retained recovery source is suppressed solely by optional surplus, remaining-quota or reset-horizon targets. Required discovery accepts validated not_due evidence only when one whole account also passes ordinary availability and the intrinsic short-window reserve

Preparation outlives cancellation and retires the last attempted receipt after its hold, or before handoff while no retry was attempted; staged preparation leaves predecessors active and is itself excluded by the legacy superseded fence

Promotion revives a historical or nonempty receipt, uses changed ownership, or proceeds after a first hold; only the exact newly prepared empty row can promote under existing pool/session locks and the bounded handoff guard

Shutdown names a different receipt while promotion commits; the guard serializes first-hold recording with publication and commit of conservative attempt intent, while timeout or indeterminate work retains uncertainty

Incomplete receipt history or a live predecessor can release capacity unsafely; the native two-dispatch proof bounds complete history before the first POST, observes every guest terminal, and revalidates the identical locked chain and quiescent owner before exact capacity-only settlement

Requiring terminal time after the local restore error rejects an already-terminal dispatch or drain continuation; complete terminal-before-dispatch or bounded all-guests-terminal chain proof releases only capacity, without granting retry authority

Retrying without room for all remaining roles or with obsolete authority exceeds the original task; pre-pause and atomic grant checks reserve the original turns and cost ceilings, bind exact machine pause and rollout, and authorize one 1-to-2 renewal only

Reusing a repaired-task grant after its 30-minute deadline or renewing it again would prolong authority; effective-policy dispatch and publication deadlines plus the single authorization and exact graph renewal prevent further starts or output

Accepting a supplied actor, untyped review or incomplete file evidence could authorize unapproved effects; standing-human access, actor-bound preview/apply, server-derived Git proof and typed exact-head review bind the audited decision

Replaying revocation against a replacement grant or deleting explicit authority could revoke unrelated consent or expose a machine fallback; the locked operation targets one authorization audit and retains a tombstone with actor-scoped idempotency

Reusing approval after an uncertain queue request or ejection could grant another factory arming attempt; an intent commits before external I/O and the same authorization cannot reserve a second attempt, while queue observations bind the first observed entry

unsafe_feedback.signal: claimed_by_replica + claimed_at lease row
unsafe_feedback.condition: A pod's own clock running ahead of the database's is the dangerous skew direction named in the reclaim function's own docstring: it sees a live claim as older than it is and reclaims a turn that is still being actively executed by its true owner. NTP keeps this far inside the 30s lease in practice, but the failure is explicitly documented as silent

unsafe_feedback.signal: feature grant rows for guild+subject+scope
unsafe_feedback.condition: A revoked or newly added grant is not seen for up to the 30s cache TTL, so the ACL authorizes on old policy

unsafe_feedback.signal: leader_lease.heartbeat_at freshness
unsafe_feedback.condition: A leader whose event loop stalls past the 5s TTL (e.g. a sync Session call in async) is stolen from while still holding live singletons, so two replicas run them

unsafe_feedback.signal: observability topology/stats snapshot rows
unsafe_feedback.condition: If the Argo rollup stops, the public stats endpoint can serve an old snapshot without an age field or freshness error

unsafe_feedback.signal: run-accepted / result acknowledgement from the EmberVM shim invoke
unsafe_feedback.condition: A read timeout raised as EmberVMTimeout leaves the monolith unable to confirm whether the guest actually started or is still running the turn; the pending row is deleted and the turn recorded as a terminal error either way, so a caller who resubmits the same prompt can produce a second guest-side run for what they perceive as one request

unsafe_feedback.signal: stdout/stderr/exit_code/files for a (language, code) key
unsafe_feedback.condition: The Idempotency-Key hashes only language and code, not the optional input files; EmberVM's task store dedupes a resubmit against the existing task's stored result for its result TTL (CRD default 86400s, not overridden for the sandbox workloads), so a caller who resubmits identical code with different input files within that window silently receives the first submission's output computed against the first submission's files. Shotter had the identical bug (a URL-only key colliding across distinct captures) and was fixed by switching to a random per-call nonce; that fix's own comment explains a params-derived key is only correct when EVERY input that affects the result is part of the key, which this key does not satisfy

unsafe_feedback.signal: content-addressed screenshot URL + stored flag in tool metadata
unsafe_feedback.condition: put_screenshot derives the URL before the R2 PUT and returns it even on failure; _meta.stored=false reports failure while inline PNG bytes remain available. A caller ignoring stored can retain an absent-object pointer. Even stored=true proves only a successful PUT, not authenticated GET access, URL durability or bucket retention

unsafe_feedback.signal: X-Auth-Email identity header
unsafe_feedback.condition: The header is forwarded by several allowlisted in-cluster senders behind a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy, but the policy narrows WHO can reach the pod, not whether the value each of those senders sends is itself verified; the only current consumer records it as attribution with no authorization decision resting on it, so the gap is dormant rather than exploitable today, but nothing in the code enforces that boundary if a future authorization check starts keying on the header directly instead of verifying the underlying JWT

unsafe_feedback.signal: Healthy, known failure or unknown backup advisory result
unsafe_feedback.condition: Absent, unreadable or older-than-two-hour snapshots produce status unknown, which preserves the last announced state and cannot falsely recover an alert, but also cannot send a checker-absence alert or repeat a previously failing backup alert while evidence remains unavailable; operators must inspect private health detail and CronJob failures

unsafe_feedback.signal: Current can_start control subgate and observation coverage
unsafe_feedback.condition: Separate database reads can race with holds, funding or execution changes; treating an earlier positive subgate as a complete dispatch decision skips transport, quota and physical-capacity checks. Coverage explicitly marks those gates unevaluated and recovery_authorized remains false; execution must still use its existing fresh controls

unsafe_feedback.signal: Unknown control result or unavailable canonical identity
unsafe_feedback.condition: Missing identity, malformed evidence or an unrecognized control reason cannot establish that a reconciliation tick ran, that execution never started or that a guest ceased. Substituting a recovery decision for the returned unknown state can duplicate work; the projection returns ok null and grants no recovery authority

unsafe_feedback.signal: Latest funding request, settlement and grant audit identities with request relationship
unsafe_feedback.condition: The latest settlement or grant can belong to older funding history; treating its presence as settlement of the latest request or as a current execution decision loses lineage. The projection exposes audit identities, requires the settlement request_id to match the latest request audit_id, preserves different-request pending state and returns unavailable for malformed linkage

unsafe_feedback.signal: Standing decision and durable policy-transition identity
unsafe_feedback.condition: Comparing only restored policy bytes would resurrect a grant; the binding includes the latest successful or indeterminate policy event, excluding explicit failures and proven landing-toggle no-ops while identical command replay creates no new authority

unsafe_feedback.signal: Standing decision and durable policy-transition identity
unsafe_feedback.condition: A later successful or indeterminate transition invalidates repair authority even if policy bytes are restored; latest_policy_transition must retain legacy outcome-absent events and distinguish failed/no-op/replayed commands from transitions

unsafe_feedback.signal: Task/start quiescence and claimed PendingMessage ownership
unsafe_feedback.condition: Terminal graph/start records alone can conceal a still-claimed session; the shared execution_refusal checks claimed messages as well as native quiescence for the delivery and applicable source/canonical history without inferring cessation or resetting claims

unsafe_feedback.signal: Absence-of-hold observation inside an accepted native brief
unsafe_feedback.condition: A substring match on leave-unmerged reverses the meaning of the two observed complete absence assertions. The shared classifier suppresses only those exact assertions in unqualified prose, keeps remaining matches as vetoes and is exercised with both complete live briefs through receive and late hold checks

unsafe_feedback.signal: Positive, quoted, conditional or otherwise qualified hold text alongside an absence observation
unsafe_feedback.condition: Skipping an entire brief, trusting its heading or author, or ignoring a positive match elsewhere could lose a hold. The classifier has no provenance exemption; other matches, quoted, retracted and qualifying context remain refusals, and native landing rechecks the same predicate before arming and while observing queued work

unsafe_feedback.signal: Per-account window permission for required discovery
unsafe_feedback.condition: A lone short window has no longer companion and can pass relative preview checks with less than 10 percent remaining. After full preview validation, reported durations at or below 300 minutes retain the same reserve independently of names; account rows are never combined and configured ordinary availability still binds

unsafe_feedback.signal: Fresh complete broker observation and later permitted evidence
unsafe_feedback.condition: Stale, future, partial, malformed, exhausted or pacing-restricted evidence cannot permit discovery. A forced broker read and existing preview plus ordinary freshness checks refuse without consuming the source; a later permitting observation retries the same event through the normal cadence

unsafe_feedback.signal: Prepared versus attempted phase and compatibility fence
unsafe_feedback.condition: A mixed-version reader mistakes preparation for execution evidence or a legacy callback makes it promotable; prepared rows remain superseded, new callbacks refuse before promotion, nonempty rows cannot promote and legacy NULL behavior is unchanged; the callback observer waits for successful promotion before using the unchanged active-owner reader

unsafe_feedback.signal: Cancelled worker or lost promotion commit response
unsafe_feedback.condition: An asyncio waiter disappears while its worker can still commit; pending intent suppresses zero-execution settlement, publication precedes commit, and late work rechecks exact claim, permit and first-hold fences without authorizing another POST

unsafe_feedback.signal: Retained physical POST receipts and current ownership
unsafe_feedback.condition: A fresh second dispatch cannot prove older receipt retention; native drain proof requires session and permit age within retention, complete bounded enumeration including superseded identities, finished observers, fresh terminal observations for every guest and an unchanged chain under locks

unsafe_feedback.signal: Original allocation, exact pause/resume, rollout and node renewal
unsafe_feedback.condition: Authority or accounting may change after grant; physical admission reauthenticates the grant and all remaining-role reservations, excludes its own exact reservation once, and refuses other unknown starts, changed holds, decision state or rollout

unsafe_feedback.signal: Current base ref, immutable merge base and complete regular-file manifest
unsafe_feedback.condition: Stale PR base metadata, omitted files or unsupported object kinds could hide an approved diff change; proof reads the actual branch ref, reconstructs changed Git trees, verifies bounded UTF-8 blob identities and confirms immutable inputs against the audited manifest

unsafe_feedback.signal: Independent review identity, artifact digest, typed scope and operator effect acknowledgements
unsafe_feedback.condition: An untyped, replaced or stale review could conceal required operator effects; the explicit grant binds native review run/session identity, artifact digest, merge base and exact paths, checks every acknowledged true effect and revalidates before arming and queued observation

non_ucas.item: a rendered public doc linking out to a non-public repository document
non_ucas.reason: buildPathIndex only maps allowlisted manifest paths to slugs; a link to anything else is stripped to plain text rather than left live (projects/monolith/frontend/src/lib/server/docs.js:9)

non_ucas.item: a repeat POST of the same shotter.capture request colliding across two unrelated captures
non_ucas.reason: Fixed: the Idempotency-Key is now a random per-call nonce, so it only buys transport-retry safety within one call and cannot collapse two distinct captures of the same URL onto one cached result (projects/monolith/shotter/client.py:82)

non_ucas.item: a repo doc outside the seven PUBLIC_PROJECTS directories reaching the docs manifest
non_ucas.reason: The generator indexes only exact path matches built from a fixed PUBLIC_PROJECTS x DOC_KINDS product, not a directory walk, so nothing else in the repo, including ADRs and nested READMEs, is reachable through this generator regardless of what git ls-files returns (projects/monolith/knowledge/tools/gen_docs_manifest.py:49)

non_ucas.item: a single missed leadership heartbeat
non_ucas.reason: Bounded by 2s renew inside the 5s TTL, and any error resolves to follower fail-safe (projects/monolith/core/leadership.py:29)

non_ucas.item: an ungated docs/posts draft (no public key, or public: false) reaching the public site
non_ucas.reason: Fails closed: _declared_public_value returns None for an ungated file and it is skipped, and a strict literal-match check on the public key raises rather than guessing (projects/monolith/knowledge/tools/gen_posts_manifest.py:64)

non_ucas.item: outbox at-least-once duplicate on crash between post and mark
non_ucas.reason: Bounded and mostly idempotent: reactions/edits resolve missing targets, a duplicate notify is a rare nuisance (projects/monolith/chat/outbox.py:135)

non_ucas.item: public_reader denied on a private schema
non_ucas.reason: Not a hazard but the enforced control: DB permission denies the read; asserted by projects/monolith/public_reader_grants_test.py:44

non_ucas.item: scheduler.trigger submits the wrong execution path
non_ucas.reason: Bounded by run-now looking up the CronWorkflow whose `replaces` annotation names the requested job and creating a one-off Workflow from its `workflowSpec`; `ARGO_JOBS` only suppresses legacy registry metadata, including for suspended entries (projects/monolith/scheduler/service.py:53)

non_ucas.item: shotter.capture exceeding its render budget
non_ucas.reason: Bounded by the nested timeout chain (Context Forge 60s > client read 55s > workload 50s > guest handler 45s > CDP navigate), converted into a ToolTimeout rather than an indefinite hold (projects/monolith/shotter/client.py:96)

non_ucas.item: two replicas racing to claim the same pending message
non_ucas.reason: claim_pending_message_for_session_sync is a single atomic UPDATE ... WHERE claimed_by_replica IS NULL, so only one of two concurrent claimants can succeed (projects/monolith/factory/execution/store.py:634)

non_ucas.item: apply_extraction re-running on a raw that already extracted successfully
non_ucas.reason: Guarded by an early replayed-check keyed on (raw_fk, gardener_version, non-failed provenance) that returns before writing any atom (projects/monolith/knowledge/extraction.py:326)

non_ucas.item: the kg daily-cap deferral calling both finish_drainer_job and defer_drainer_job for the same one-shot job
non_ucas.reason: complete_job's NULL next_run_at write for a one-shot row (interval_secs IS NULL) is immediately overwritten by defer_job's later write in the same call sequence, so the job still re-arms at +3600s despite the double write (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/drainer.py:407)

non_ucas.item: report_distress's Discord notification failing without the reporting agent knowing
non_ucas.reason: notify() failure is caught and reflected honestly in the returned status (recorded vs notified), and the underlying enqueue reuses the durable at-least-once outbox row already covered by the existing outbox non_uca (projects/monolith/knowledge/mcp.py:446)

non_ucas.item: Luna claiming verification_state=verified with no evidence array
non_ucas.reason: apply_extraction force-downgrades to unverified server-side whenever assertion.evidence is empty, regardless of what the model claimed (projects/monolith/knowledge/extraction.py:364)

non_ucas.item: an absent, malformed, future-dated or failed-export observation falsely clearing a backup alert
non_ucas.reason: evaluate_cnpg_backups validates target identity and timestamps, rejects observations over 7200 seconds old, and requires successful export for every healthy target; decide skips unknown before changing the durable state (projects/monolith/factory/ops_health.py:664, projects/monolith/factory/health_alerts.py:110).

non_ucas.item: a new cluster with no successful base backup being reported healthy because its creation age is small
non_ucas.reason: A false has_successful_backup with a null successful-backup timestamp always produces a known failure, including age zero; successful backups become failures strictly after 129600 seconds, recomputed between checker runs (projects/monolith/factory/ops_health.py:703).

non_ucas.item: one unreadable target masking a known failed backup on another target
non_ucas.reason: The checker records each target independently and the evaluator returns known failures before unknowns; the 120-second job deadline bounds at most four targets (projects/platform/otel-collector/files/backup_check.py:206, projects/monolith/factory/ops_health.py:722, projects/platform/otel-collector/templates/backup-check.yaml:147).

non_ucas.item: backup degradation restarting monolith or making public health fail
non_ucas.reason: The check is registered only as private advisory health and liveness stays /healthz; composition tests assert private health HTTP 200, unchanged kubelet liveness and no public backup component (projects/monolith/factory/module.py:174, projects/monolith/factory/module_test.py:72).

non_ucas.item: normal leader handover resending the last backup transition on every new leader
non_ucas.reason: The transition notifier reads platform_probe state and persists only after enqueue; normal handover deduplicates, while the existing enqueue-before-latch crash window can produce an at-least-once duplicate and is not claimed exactly-once (projects/monolith/factory/health_alerts.py:58, projects/monolith/factory/health_alerts.py:137).

non_ucas.item: the rendered checker acquiring broad CNPG privileges or writing application status through a public route
non_ucas.reason: Per-namespace Roles grant get only on configured Cluster resourceNames, and a separate Role grants get/patch only on one ConfigMap; no ClusterRole or application write route is introduced. Live additive bindings remain an explicit acceptance check (projects/platform/otel-collector/templates/backup-check.yaml:55, docs/observability.md, #7002).

non_ucas.item: refill starting from a stale or incomplete low-backlog observation
non_ucas.reason: Omission is inert. Enabled starts require complete evidence within the discovery refresh window, current policy, ordinary capacity, charter ownership and cooldown; an existing unsettled run prevents another reservation (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill.py:180).

non_ucas.item: a refill worker broadening its task into a second delivery workflow
non_ucas.reason: New starts pin read-only collection and independent Astra review nodes with separate structured contracts. Legacy starts retain their original inventory contract. Transport checks bind receipt, generation, policy digest, exact role, attempt and model; only the trusted producer can publish evidence-approved plans (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_worker.py: reconcile; backlog_refill.py: _dispatch_allowed; backlog_refill_producer.py: collection and review).

non_ucas.item: an owner pause, cancellation or deadline change during discovery authorizing a new issue POST
non_ucas.reason: The producer rechecks the owning admitted receipt, pause/cancellation state, generation, policy and deadline under the control lock immediately before committing the intent, after discovery I/O (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_producer.py:68, projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_producer.py:150).

non_ucas.item: a lost GitHub POST response causing either a duplicate POST or a permanently fenced refill run
non_ucas.reason: An intent commits before POST and is never resent. Six read-only attempts quarantine only the output; the run can settle inconclusive while one due original output per maintenance tick continues daily marker reconciliation, including while disabled (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_producer.py:150, projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_producer.py:112, projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_producer.py:321).

non_ucas.item: a rolling daily refill limit becoming a permanent human reset gate
non_ucas.reason: The limit counts all starts in the rolling 24-hour window, including unresolved starts, and automatically permits another reservation when the window has room; it does not open a breaker (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill.py:180).

non_ucas.item: routine cancellation or a paused task deadline poisoning the refill failure streak
non_ucas.reason: Terminal interrupted runs settle inconclusive after unresolved execution drains. Inconclusive outcomes neither advance nor reset failure or low-yield streaks; conclusive settlements are recorded once (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_worker.py:88, projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill.py:298).

non_ucas.item: a model renaming a finding key to count the same title as fresh yield
non_ucas.reason: The producer derives cross-run finding identity from the normalized title and counts only confirmed newly created issues. This conservatively matches titles; semantic duplicate detection is outside this check (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_producer.py:301, projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill_producer.py:321).

non_ucas.item: accepting a saved finish grants another execution after the task deadline
non_ucas.reason: The expired-lease saved-finish path verifies existing evidence before funding or dispatch. It rechecks the control, complete graph/run identity, quiescence, owned PR current head, CI and independent review under settlement locks. It neither changes deadlines nor admits work (factory/orchestration/factory_conductor.py: _adopt_saved_finish).

non_ucas.item: recording a draft-only hold renews a task lease or fabricates landing authority
non_ucas.reason: An exact operator landing_hold-only amendment records the restrictive typed hold and audit without a funding grant, deadline, budget or graph change. Draft acceptance requires that existing hold; saved free text never creates one, and the hold survives settlement (factory/orchestration/factory_policy_amendment.py: _preview and apply; factory_conductor.py: _adopt_saved_finish).

non_ucas.item: an enqueue_extraction failure inside persist_raw_with_status leaving an extractable raw unqueued
non_ucas.reason: The savepoint rolls back only the job insert; sweep_unqueued_raws re-registers any extractable raw with no job, no handled provenance and no exhausted failure at the start of every drain_cycle with the kg kind enabled (projects/monolith/knowledge/raw_write.py:139, projects/monolith/knowledge/extraction.py:399, projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/drainer.py:1792)

non_ucas.item: the ember-session feed advancing its watermark past a turn range whose extraction job was never registered
non_ucas.reason: Fixed: _feed_once_sync re-enqueues an existing unqueued raw and leaves kg_extracted_turn_seq unchanged unless the raw is queued or handled (projects/monolith/factory/execution/kg_feed.py:335)

non_ucas.item: a malformed-output extraction failure dead-lettering after one attempt
non_ucas.reason: Fixed: ExtractionOutputInvalid takes the same _retry_or_dead_letter_kg path as other failures, which defers the job while attempts stay below MAX_GARDENER_RETRIES and records the failure only after that (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/drainer.py:2164)

non_ucas.item: a KG-lane dead letter with no operator path back to extraction
non_ucas.reason: GET /api/knowledge/dead-letter lists raws at MAX_GARDENER_RETRIES; replay deletes the failed provenance row, reopens resolution_failed disputes and re-enqueues extraction (projects/monolith/knowledge/router.py:541)

non_ucas.item: a dead-lettered dispute leaving its note flagged disputed
non_ucas.reason: Conservative: _record_failure moves an exhausted dispute to resolution_failed, which open_dispute_note_ids still counts as unresolved, so callers keep treating the fact as contested until replay reopens it (projects/monolith/knowledge/extraction.py:651, projects/monolith/knowledge/store.py:93)

non_ucas.item: removing an unused receipt model renews an expired task or grants execution
non_ucas.reason: The standing-operator removal mode requires a paused, quiescent receipt, rejects mixed fields, current model choices and empty pools, and updates only the receipt restriction, control version and idempotent audit. Funding grants, expired deadlines, pause, holds and historical pins remain unchanged (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_policy_amendment.py:35 and :277).

non_ucas.item: a historical session dispatches a removed receipt model after a separate resume
non_ucas.reason: Native pre-delivery and physical admission pass the actual normalized PendingMessage model to factory_session_allowed. Restricted receipts refuse removed or unpinned models, including same-family overrides, while historical session models and results remain unchanged (projects/monolith/factory/execution/mcp.py:1164 and :1196; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/api.py:74).

non_ucas.item: operator chat or decision requeue silently restores a removed receipt model
non_ucas.reason: The direction builder preserves model_restriction through same-receipt requeue. Fresh admission filters the effective policy and refuses conflicting scalar defaults or empty pools before creating a new task. Existing continuation compares the effective policy while retaining stale-revision and nonrenewable-recovery fences (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_decisions.py:1033; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_intake.py:860; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_continuations.py:81).

non_ucas.item: a stale or repeated removal preview changes unrelated receipt authority
non_ucas.reason: The preview binds control version, graph revision and state, receipt direction, accounting and funding/recovery identities. Apply rechecks under control/task locks and returns the recorded result for an identical request key, with a conflict refusing changed arguments (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_policy_amendment.py:35 and :277).

non_ucas.item: quota becoming unavailable or authority changing before a refill role reaches transport
non_ucas.reason: Each new role checks its exact offered model against fresh subscription windows without fallback. Durable ownership, policy, pause and deadline gates are checked again after broker I/O. The safe-control preview and apply each observe both generator and Astra quota (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/backlog_refill.py: quota and _dispatch_allowed; refill_control.py: _observations and _plan).

non_ucas.item: the explicitly authorized Codex worker and drainer reserve change implicitly enabling paid fallback or clearing execution holds
non_ucas.reason: Joe approved both shared role floors at 8 percent on 2026-10-31. Only swarm.quotaFloors.codex.worker and .drainer change in deploy/values-gke.yaml, reaching model_pool.floor_for through SWARM_QUOTA_FLOORS. The drainer floor covers general and knowledge jobs, including hourly learning; implementation retains 10 percent and other providers retain their floors. Existing grant selection, subscription billing, capacity and daily caps, freshness checks, refill breaker, receipt holds and unknown-execution fences are unchanged (chart/templates/deployment.yaml; factory/orchestration/model_pool.py: availability; drainer.py: provider_walled and claim_drainer_job; backlog_refill.py: quota).

non_ucas.item: native registration feedback being mistaken for caller exposure or execution authority
non_ucas.reason: Operator-only factory_status reports native source and explicitly unobserved caller visibility for two existing controls. It does not refresh catalogues or mutate authority. The authenticated flow retains separate restriction and continuation previews, exact identity bindings, fresh quota, holds and uncertain-execution guards (factory/orchestration/mcp.py and factory_operator_flow_test.py).

non_ucas.item: a missing historical guest row being treated as proof that an unknown learning invocation never ran
non_ucas.reason: A typed missing projection selects only a bounded authenticated journal verifier; incomplete or stale proof and successor ownership refuse acknowledgement, while the failed unknown turn and accounting remain unchanged (projects/monolith/factory/learning_reconciliation.py).

non_ucas.item: Retire a delivered Claude quota probe binding only after exact positive terminal evidence
non_ucas.reason: The bounded leader retry binds the origin audit, sole completed turn and settled permit, receipt provenance, dispatch and original-generation destroyed guest. A fresh authenticated read is rechecked under control/capacity/session/receipt locks; changed identities, aliases, pending work, missing evidence and unknown outcomes refuse. Fence and binding retirement commit with one audit, preserve result/accounting/lineage and observer timestamps, and perform neither DELETE nor inference. Evidence: factory/completed_probe_cleanup.py; factory/execution/guest_cleanup.py.

non_ucas.item: An uninvoked retry is mistaken for proof that an earlier missing dispatch never ran
non_ucas.reason: Explicit operator recovery requires an empty exact first receipt, released observer, unchanged terminal workflow and native ownership. The CP must independently prove positive idled parking and complete journal/successor coverage, then durably fence that original lineage against restore. Digest/CAS and audited intent bind replay; the final lock rechecks local identity and preserves the native turn, settled permit, unknown result, reserved cost and unrelated holds. Partial remote effects remain explicit, never a success or a zero-cost refund. Evidence: projects/monolith/factory/settled_retry_reconciliation.py; factory/execution/reconciliation.py:read_unknown_retry_factory_attempt.

non_ucas.item: factory-start-diagnostics: a positive read granting dispatch or recovery authority
non_ucas.reason: The helper only observes the existing can_start subgate under no_autoflush and emits recovery_authorized false. It neither calls transport or provider paths nor claims, resumes or changes a queued turn; the exact-session regression preserves the latent pending message for both positive and negative gate results (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_start_diagnostics.py:91,176,233; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/mcp_test.py:371,480).

non_ucas.item: factory-start-diagnostics: a loosely matching session exporting another attempt as current
non_ucas.reason: Canonical task, node and positive attempt syntax must agree with the session workflow and node metadata, the exact durable run session/dispatch identity and a receipt. Missing or conflicting identity returns unknown before can_start is called; no correction or execution permission is inferred (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_start_diagnostics.py:243; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/mcp_test.py:430).

non_ucas.item: factory-start-diagnostics: funding history leaking private plans or expanding reads with audit history
non_ucas.reason: Latest request, settlement and grant reads use exact-task action filters and LIMIT 1. The projection emits bounded identifiers, validated timestamps, finite failure categories and flags, verifies a source run belongs to the task, and excludes plan, direction and refusal prose; history-growth and no-write regressions cover the observational contract (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_start_diagnostics.py:107,116; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/mcp_test.py:314,480,504).

non_ucas.item: identical grant replay or a fresh standing authorization replenishing cumulative derivations
non_ucas.reason: Exact candidate replay is free. Distinct owner grants count by canonical repository/PR across receipts and authorizations; ongoing repair grants count by repair and source tasks across authorizations, with a separate rolling rate bound (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/owner_pr_landing_delegation.py:705; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/repair_landing_delegation.py:555).

non_ucas.item: machine delegation replacing an explicit human grant or falling through to another delegate
non_ucas.reason: delegation_owner returns no delegate whenever landing_authorization exists, including malformed authority. Owner-marked receipts select only the owner delegate; refusal cannot fall through to repair authority (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_landing_release.py:346).

non_ucas.item: an unrelated main advance invalidating an identical reviewed diff
non_ucas.reason: Delegation compares the review's immutable merge base and exact head/path evidence rather than persisting mutable PR base.sha. Changed comparison evidence still refuses (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/owner_pr_landing_delegation.py:653; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/repair_landing_delegation.py:466).

non_ucas.item: factory-owner-hold-text: recognizing an absence assertion grants scope or releases a durable hold
non_ucas.reason: The pure shared text predicate adds no authority fields or database writes. Native receive retains canonical ownership and history checks; exact-head review, CI, explicit landing authorization, security and credential boundaries remain their existing owners (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/owner_prs.py:556; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_intake_loop_test.py:4270; factory_landing_test.py:3422).

non_ucas.item: factory-owner-hold-text: a parser fix erases a cached discussion refusal or a pending owner
non_ucas.reason: No historical comment, audit, cache or receipt is rewritten. The existing 24-hour exact-PR-update refusal cache keeps its expiry and fresh observation path; existing queued, paused, cancelled and uncertain histories still exclude competing delivery (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/owner_prs.py:455; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_intake_loop_test.py:4354 and test_owner_pr_preserves_receipt_history_across_generations).

non_ucas.item: factory-required-recovery: a permitted discovery observation authorizes paid execution
non_ucas.reason: Discovery only publishes a bounded issue. Existing intake, model/account routing, paid-start admission, receipt ownership, explicit holds and uncertain-execution fences remain their owners; native regression asserts no receipt admission, FactoryStart or node attempt is created. Optional scout and companion-window pacing behavior are unchanged (factory/orchestration/factory_problem_issues.py:83,964; factory_problem_issues_test.py: test_native_required_discovery_waits_for_single_window_reserve).

non_ucas.item: factory-required-recovery: fresh quota resets a historical event or bypasses publication bounds
non_ucas.reason: A refused quota observation skips the two recovery sources without changing their policy watermark or terminal history. A later permitting observation publishes the same source ID once under existing per-tick and rolling caps, deduplication, nonrecursive ownership and uncertain-write reconciliation (factory/orchestration/factory_problem_issues.py:564,938,964; factory_problem_issues_test.py: test_native_required_discovery_uses_ordinary_quota_with_existing_bounds and test_native_required_discovery_waits_for_single_window_reserve).

non_ucas.item: A diagnostic error, historical breaker or unknown invocation must not grant a repair retry
non_ucas.reason: Only two fresh distinct-task, exact native not-invoked proofs with allowlisted staged database metadata can produce the existing machine pause. The start's version and control epoch exclude historical work and policy disable/restore; permission/authentication failures are not repairable inputs.

non_ucas.item: A closed issue must not become generic execution authority
non_ucas.reason: Only native charter #7366's exact recurring receipt and synchronized mirror may remain closed, with current ownership/hold checks at producer, funding, physical dispatch and settlement. Repair issues retain their ordinary open-source requirement.

non_ucas.item: A model must not choose a funding execution profile or mutate its request
non_ucas.reason: The funding owner hashes request, prompt and schema into its admitted identity, verifies session/model at dispatch, and rejects stale or mismatched artifacts. Generic gate/read-only exceptions remain closed. Unsupported adapters cannot fall back to repository execution or explicit PR-review credentials.

non_ucas.item: Funding content must not reach a CLI before its capabilities are known
non_ucas.reason: The pinned CLI's pre-input initialize response does not declare tools, so the decision profile never starts it. Subscription OAuth must not authenticate a bespoke Messages client. Native funding scheduling and physical starts are disabled, and the guest independently refuses before HTTP construction. No policy or ambient credential enables the route. Future dedicated API-key authority must bind the exact profile, request and dispatch before content is forwarded. Tests that mock that future route confer no production authority.

non_ucas.item: A repair ticket must not invent an owning scope or landing authority
non_ucas.reason: Only reauthenticated native evidence selects fixed role, stage, SQLSTATE and paths; private identifiers and raw SQL/errors remain private. Execution admission and result-receipt repairs are outside the standing landing profiles and must retain `repair_landing_paths_require_operator`. Post-operator rollout fixtures cannot establish autonomous native landing reachability.

non_ucas.item: Rollout is necessary but insufficient: the funding grant retains original accounting and exact repair binding, permits only attempt two, and expires
non_ucas.reason: Useful publication requires the fixed independent reviewer. Producer recovery observation waits for that publication, not merely a successful node or grant. Regression evidence is synthetic; independent security-aware exact-head review and real operational acceptance remain pending.

non_ucas.item: an expired or revoked operator grant silently falling back to standing delegation
non_ucas.reason: Explicit authority remains in landing_authorization. Revocation targets its audit and retains a tombstone; scoped_refusal refuses it before delegate selection. Replay only acknowledges the prior request, and a new grant requires a fresh authenticated preview/apply (projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/factory_landing_release.py; projects/monolith/factory/orchestration/operator_landing_authorization.py:448).

open_questions: How should the native ingress successor cover Context Forge and direct-mount callers after #5816 removed the inert Cilium ingress template?

Does any workload other than shotter and the six sandbox languages share the same EmberVM Idempotency-Key-from-request-parameters pattern, and if so does its key cover every parameter that affects the result?
In production, can a chat message handler (LLM summarizer) exceed the 30s message-lock TTL under load and trip lock.reclaim.wrong-timing, or is processing reliably shorter?

Is the X-Auth-Email header ever going to gate an authorization decision, or does #4940's delegation model deliberately avoid keying on inbound headers at all? If the latter, header-authz-drift can be downgraded once that is documented somewhere durable.

What are the effective R2 shotter bucket read grants and lifecycle rules? The chart configures an HTTPS S3 endpoint and secret-backed signed client; shotter emits an unsigned endpoint URL with no read proxy or presigning. Network reachability and a content hash alone do not establish read authorization, and the repository proves no object retention duration (projects/monolith/shotter/s3.py:59; projects/monolith/core/s3.py:26; projects/monolith/chart/templates/deployment.yaml:595).
How should finer tool-specific entitlements constrain shotter.capture, sandbox.run and cluster mutations within the current shared operators gate (#6475)?

The framework is now built, but strict per-domain schema isolation and the cross-domain contract are still conventions. Re-run this analysis when those controls become enforceable rather than merely compositional.

The private chart enables HPA from 1 to 3 replicas; verify claim-lease behavior under real scale-out and termination, especially whether a terminating pod's in-flight claims are released promptly enough for the 30s lease to matter in practice.

The public backend has a deliberate primary write path and public FaaS invocation path. Confirm production database grants and service-account permissions match the chart claims: public_writer must remain limited to chat_public, and the public service account must remain identity-only with no Kubernetes RBAC. The removed Cilium templates provide no replacement network enforcement; that remains separate work under #5276 and #5277.

When the scratch-Postgres feature is re-enabled (embervm side), should run_code's docstring be corrected to stop claiming zero network for python, or should the DSN injection move behind a separate, explicitly-network-capable tool so the isolation claim stays true for the tool most callers reach for?

#7002: verify fresh successful-backup timestamps, scheduled checker completion, metric/advisory arrival, runtime ConfigMap preservation and effective additive RBAC on the hub; live Cluster/RBAC reads and Honeycomb queries were unavailable to this activation session. Checker-absence notifications remain outside the current advisory contract.

Default-off refill live acceptance remains on #7376: verify ordinary intake, inventory outputs, a restart and ambiguous-write drill, breaker reset, rolling-limit recovery and disable reconciliation before enablement.

Revocation cannot undo an already completed GitHub merge. The native observer disarms/dequeues on its next tick, and failed external calls retain errors for observation; confirm this external-action boundary during parent-owned operational acceptance (#7601, #7597). Explicit operator expiry and revocation have the same asynchronous limit: GitHub may merge before the next successful observation, and unobserved external requeue races cannot be ruled out by a polling fence. A stronger final-action guarantee needs a trusted required queue check or final merge owner.
